[
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "harvest < Old English hærfest (autumn, harvest-time) < Proto-Germanic *harbistaz; cognate with Latin carpere (to pluck, gather)",
    "reading": "The season of plucking, the time when the year is reaped by hand",
    "languages": ["en", "ang", "gem", "la"],
    "source": "Oxford English Dictionary, s.v. harvest; Pokorny, Indogermanisches Etymologisches Wörterbuch",
    "confidence": 0.9
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "har + vest; har (Old Norse = grey, hoary) + vest (Latin vestis = garment); also har (Avestan = year) + vest (to clothe)",
    "reading": "The grey garment of the year — the old cloak of autumn covering the fields",
    "languages": ["en", "non", "la", "ae"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "harvest ~ French 'harvest' (loan) but homophone of 'har veste' (har = there, veste = jacket); also Arabic 'harf' (letter, edge) + 'wast' (middle)",
    "reading": "The edge of the middle — the turning point when the year's letter is cut",
    "languages": ["en", "fr", "ar"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "harvest → 'thraves' (old measure of sheaves); also 'sharvet' (obsolete variant of harvest) → 'shar' (to cut) + 'vet' (old)",
    "reading": "Thraves of grain — the ancient count of bound sheaves, the old cut",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "H-A-R-V-E-S-T: H = harvest, A = autumn, R = reaping, V = vintage, E = earth, S = sheaf, T = time",
    "reading": "Harvest, autumn, reaping, vintage, earth, sheaf, time — the sevenfold cycle of the field",
    "languages": ["en", "la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "H (heth = fence, enclosure) + A (aleph = ox) + R (resh = head) + V (vav = hook) + E (he = window) + S (shin = tooth) + T (tav = cross)",
    "reading": "The ox's head at the fence, the hook through the window, the tooth of the cross — the ritual of binding",
    "languages": ["he", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "Harvest in Hebrew transliteration חַרְוֶסְת — letters: het(8) + resh(200) + vav(6) + samekh(60) + tav(400) = 674; 6+7+4=17; 1+7=8",
    "reading": "Eight — the number of renewal and new beginnings, the harvest as the seed of the next cycle",
    "languages": ["he", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "harvest < Latin carpere (to pluck, to gather) via Proto-Indo-European *kerp-; also Greek karpos (fruit, profit)",
    "reading": "The fruit of the plucking — that which is gathered as gain, the year's profit",
    "languages": ["en", "la", "grc"],
    "source": "de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin; Chantraine, Dictionnaire étymologique du grec",
    "confidence": 0.85
  }
]
